content.text:
Audit complete; no files changed.

Current state:

- `mobile/src/lib/types.ts` now has an attachment scaffold (`ChatAttachment`, URI plus transient `data`) at lines 6–29, but the provider transport remains text-only.
- `buildProviderRequest()` serializes every turn as `message.content: string` for all four provider paths ([provider-client.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/provider-client.ts:54), [provider-client.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/provider-client.ts:86)).
- The web adapter sends images as native Pi `ImageContent`, but converts both text files and PDFs into text; PDFs are locally extracted and scanned PDFs are rejected ([AssistantChatPanel.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/components/AssistantChatPanel.tsx:398), [AssistantChatPanel.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/components/AssistantChatPanel.tsx:2802)).

Recommended persisted attachment record: `{ id, kind, name, mimeType, size, uri }`; read bytes only into a transient request object. Do not persist `data`. The current `savePersistedState(JSON.stringify(state))` would persist it despite the type comment, and the validator neither validates nor strips `attachments`.

Exact user-turn content shapes, where `B64` is raw base64 bytes, `M` is MIME type, `F` filename, and `Q` user text:

| Provider | Image | Text document | PDF |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenAI Responses | `{type:"input_image", image_url:"data:M;base64,B64", detail:"auto"}` | Prefer `{type:"input_text", text:"…decoded text…"}`; alternatively native `{type:"input_file", filename:F, file_data:B64}` | `{type:"input_file", filename:F, file_data:B64}` |
| Anthropic Messages | `{type:"image",source:{type:"base64",media_type:M,data:B64}}` | Safe universal path is `{type:"text",text:"…decoded text…"}`; reusable native file requires Files API then `{type:"document",source:{type:"file",file_id}}` | `{type:"document",source:{type:"base64",media_type:"application/pdf",data:B64}}` |
| Gemini `generateContent` | `{inlineData:{mimeType:M,data:B64}}` | `{text:"…decoded text…"}`; `inlineData` also accepts bytes but non-PDF documents are understood as text | `{inlineData:{mimeType:"application/pdf",data:B64}}` |
| OpenRouter chat | `{type:"image_url",image_url:{url:"data:M;base64,B64"}}` | `{type:"text",text:"…decoded text…"}` | `{type:"file",file:{filename:F,file_data:"data:application/pdf;base64,B64"}}` |
| Generic OpenAI-compatible chat | same `image_url` shape if model advertises vision | text only by default | no portable `file` standard—only enable OpenRouter’s `file` shape for OpenRouter or a positively known backend |

Each belongs inside one user message’s `content` array, alongside text. For example Responses uses:

```json
{
  "input": [{
    "role": "user",
    "content": [
      {"type": "input_text", "text": "Q"},
      {"type": "input_image", "image_url": "data:image/jpeg;base64,B64"},
      {"type": "input_file", "filename": "notes.pdf", "file_data": "B64"}
    ]
  }]
}
```

OpenAI documents `input_image` data URLs and `input_file` base64/file-ID inputs in Responses. [OpenAI Responses reference](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/responses/methods/create) Anthropic’s PDF and image blocks are distinct `document`/`image` content types; its Files API is the efficient persisted remote-reference option. [Anthropic PDF support](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/pdf-support), [Anthropic vision](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/vision) Gemini supports `inlineData` for both images and PDFs; inline payloads are capped by request size, so larger/reused files should use its Files API. [Gemini image input](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content/image-understanding), [Gemini document input](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content/document-processing) OpenRouter’s `file` PDF part is router-specific and can invoke paid parsing/OCR unless configured. [OpenRouter PDFs](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/overview/multimodal/pdfs), [OpenRouter images](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/overview/multimodal/image-understanding)

Implementation blockers/pitfalls:

- Attachment-only turns currently disappear: `recentMessages()` filters `message.content.trim()` and `sendMessage()` rejects blank text ([provider-client.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/provider-client.ts:54), [KeatingProvider.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/state/KeatingProvider.tsx:388)).
- Request construction is synchronous, but file bytes must be loaded from persisted app-owned URIs. Make the attachment hydration/mapping async before `fetch`; do not send stale `content://` picker URIs.
- Copy selected files into app-owned storage before persisting. `AsyncStorage` should keep only metadata/URI, not base64 (size amplification, storage limits, every historical turn otherwise re-sends bytes).
- Add a schema migration to v3 and strict attachment validation. Existing v1→v2 migration only validates `content: string` and ignores attachment fields ([persisted-state.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/persisted-state.ts:24)).
- Current mobile dependencies lack an image picker and document picker; the UI will need those acquisition paths plus MIME/size checks.
- Keep PDF native for providers that support it; the current web behavior loses page layout/charts and rejects OCR-needed scans. It is a valid fallback for text-only/custom models, not native PDF support.
- Existing web image capability guard only checks image support; add per-model file/PDF capability or a deterministic downgrade/error rather than pretending a PDF was understood natively.
- Provider history cannot be bounded only by 40 turns once binary attachments exist. Bound media count/bytes and preserve the latest attachment turn. Use provider file IDs where available for repeated turns.
- Be careful with content ordering: Anthropic recommends document/image before query text; OpenRouter recommends text first for images. Preserve per-provider ordering in mapper tests.

Tests to add:

- Extend `mobile/test/provider-client.test.ts` with a single message containing one image, UTF-8 text document, and PDF; assert all four exact wire payloads, headers/stream flags unchanged, and custom avoids unsupported PDF/file payloads.
- Cover attachment-only turn retention, 40-turn trimming with an attachment, filename/MIME propagation, and unsupported model/backend recovery text.
- Extend `mobile/test/persisted-state.test.ts` for v2→v3 migration, URI-only persistence, invalid attachment rejection, and legacy transcripts preserving no attachments.
- Test file copy/read failures and retry after a process reload using a persisted URI.
- Add an exported pure mapper or focused component test for the web adapter: image remains `ImageContent`; text document/PDF fallback content is intentional; scanned PDF produces the existing corrective error. There is currently no web attachment-adapter test—only reasoning-parser tests in `web/src/test/assistant-chat-panel.test.ts`.
- Provider-backed smoke tests should use tiny real PNG/PDF fixtures behind opt-in credentials; deterministic payload tests do not prove provider acceptance.
